clue.text: One from a special service brigade to order start of onslaught

definitions.text: One from a special service brigade

parts.note: to order is to command

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of onslaught

explanation.surface: A soldier from an elite unit is told to begin an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, a member of a special forces unit.

clue.text: Cleaner has appeal, no end

indicators.note: having no end means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: charm is attractive appeal

explanation.surface: A cleaner who is attractive, though the appeal does not last.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is British for a woman paid to clean houses; CHARM loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is an informal British word for a hired domestic cleaning woman.

clue.text: Help to support married servant

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits underneath it

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
aid is help

explanation.surface: Assistance arrives to look after a household worker who has wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic worker, a type of servant.

clue.text: Stories about male and female bringing collectible items from the US

indicators.note: the stories go around, enclosing the people named next

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
M is the abbreviation for male
Erica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Anecdotes about a man and a woman who bring home souvenirs from America.
explanation.walkthrough: Ana, originally a suffix as in Victoriana, is used as a noun for a collection of anecdotes; it splits around the man and the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and memorabilia associated with American culture, prized by collectors.

clue.text: Steer clear of the post to evade one's duties

explanation.walkthrough: A post is a column, so the literal reading is swerving round a pillar; the phrase is also an idiom for shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, originally military, means to avoid work or responsibility by staying out of the way.

clue.text: A good man in coal mine is now too old

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
taken as written
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A worthy miner underground has grown too old for the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is an idiom for someone no longer capable through age.

clue.text: Tooled up, a revolutionary crossing top of mountain

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the revolutionary straddles the next letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist

indicators.note: the top of a down-reading word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A gun-toting rebel makes a crossing over the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooled up is British slang for carrying weapons, so it means armed.

clue.text: This car ran off the rails — in this?

definitions.text: This car ran off the rails — in this?

indicators.note: something gone off the rails is out of control and disordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A carriage left the track; was it part of a disaster?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a car (railway carriage) leaving the rails is exactly what happens in this event.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage derailing is what occurs in a rail disaster, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Toys by tree dad's repackaged

indicators.note: packing contents up again lets them come out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Father's presents beside the Christmas tree are wrapped up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are soft stuffed playthings, a classic kind of children's toy.

clue.text: Make no progress dispelling new ghetto fears

indicators.note: dispelling scatters things, so these letters are dispersed and regrouped

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Efforts to ease fresh anxieties in a deprived district come to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to achieve nothing despite effort, i.e. to stall without advancing.

clue.text: Incidental remark from a subordinate

parts.note: taken as written
side as an adjective means minor or secondary, as in a side issue

explanation.surface: A junior colleague makes a passing comment.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made in passing, digressing from the main subject.

clue.text: Sleep in Happy Valley

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the state of sleep, where dreams happen
second meaning: an idyllic imaginary place of bliss

explanation.surface: Someone dozing peacefully in a pleasant valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Valley sounds like a named place, but it stands for any blissful never-never land.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the realm of slumber and an unreal paradise of perfect contentment.

clue.text: Excellent penalty, with both sides in disarray?

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty

indicators.note: a further connective sits inside those outer letters

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: one side of disarray, its first letter
the same connective, read a second time inside the outer letters
the other side of disarray, its last letter

explanation.surface: A wry cheer for a penalty handed out while both teams are in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue, hence the question mark: 'with' supplies AND, which serves twice, once after the fine and once inside the outer letters of disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and dandy is an informal idiom meaning perfectly all right or excellent.

clue.text: Tidy at university — honestly

parts.note: to put a room straight is to tidy it
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student keeps things neat while away at college, in all honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at a British university means studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is a colloquial adverb meaning truthfully, without exaggeration.

clue.text: Busy magnate bringing in staff for administration

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes the workers inside it
someone busy is bustling about, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
staff are workers, men

explanation.surface: A hard-working tycoon hires people to run the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Management means the administration of an organisation, or those who run it.

clue.text: Diadem found in Haiti, a rarity

indicators.note: the answer is discovered sitting within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the island name, the article and the start of rarity

explanation.surface: A rare jewelled headpiece turns up in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled crown or headband, the same thing as a tiara.

clue.text: US writer who ran the comic

indicators.note: comic suggests clowning about, so the letters are jumbled for laughs

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An American author who once edited a humorous magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne, author of The Scarlet Letter, was a nineteenth-century American novelist.

clue.text: Resolve, after much discussion, throwing event abroad

parts.note: the hammer throw is a field athletics event
abroad means out, away from home

explanation.surface: Officials argue at length about holding a field event overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer out a deal is to settle it through long, hard negotiation.

clue.text: An overwhelming influx in a new church in a dell

indicators.note: the second 'in' places the first group inside the valley word

parts.note: the article before dell
a vale is a valley, like a dell
the article before new
N is the abbreviation for new
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A rush of visitors descends on a newly built chapel in a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first only links the definition to the wordplay, the second is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively an avalanche is a sudden overwhelming mass of something arriving, like snow down a slope.

clue.text: Tight-fisted type causing endless hardship

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: misery is suffering or hardship

explanation.surface: A penny-pincher whose meanness brings never-ending suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending it, the very picture of stinginess.

clue.text: New record cover's for an old ballad

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
a record's cover is its sleeve; the 's is read as a plural

explanation.surface: Fresh artwork for an LP of a traditional folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is a famous Tudor English folk song, an old ballad.

clue.text: Hospital worker inside comes running over

indicators.note: turned over, the letters are read the other way
the letters are found within the next couple of words

parts.note: the tail of comes plus the start of running

explanation.surface: A medic dashes in from outside on a busy ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a member of hospital staff caring for patients.

clue.text: Lot, husband of biblical character

parts.note: a set is a lot or batch
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Lot, the Old Testament figure, is presented as someone's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot is himself a biblical figure, which tempts you to look for his relatives; here it simply means a set.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis, an Old Testament figure.

clue.text: Voice of inferior quality? Sounds like it

indicators.note: says the answer is pronounced the same as the word described

parts.note: base means low-grade or inferior

explanation.surface: Is a poor singing voice really so low? It sounds that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is the lowest male singing voice.

clue.text: Two articles about lawlessness in a region of Ukraine

indicators.note: the articles go around, enclosing what follows

parts.note: the definite article and the indefinite article
crime is lawlessness

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces report on disorder in an eastern European region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a peninsula on the Black Sea, internationally recognised as part of Ukraine.

clue.text: Oxygen needed by very great Greek character

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
mega is slang for huge or very great

explanation.surface: A tremendous figure from Greece needs air to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet; character here means a letter.

clue.text: Foremost of players, say, in a golf club

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of players
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: The leading players are named as members of a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the flat-faced club used for rolling the ball on the green.

clue.text: Sutures for small and very small people

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
titch is British slang for a tiny person

explanation.surface: Surgical threads sized for little people and even littler ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutures are surgical stitches closing a wound, so the two words are synonyms.
